title: 426. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Solving Elementary Sine Equations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Two solutions of a sine equation in one turn
questions.learningObjective: Solve a basic sine equation on one full turn in degrees.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\sin x=\frac{1}{2}\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle is \(30^\circ\). Sine is positive in Quadrants I and II, so the solutions are \(30^\circ\) and \(180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ\). The angle \(330^\circ\) is in Quadrant IV, where \(\sin 330^\circ=-\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Find the reference angle, then choose the two quadrants in which sine is positive.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a sine equation whose right side is the maximum value of sine.
questions.question: What is the solution of \(\sin x=1\) with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The sine equals \(1\) only at the top of the unit circle, where the point is \((0,1)\). This occurs at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\). At \(x=\frac{3\pi}{2}\) the point is \((0,-1)\) and the sine is \(-1\).
questions.hint: Find the point of the unit circle whose \(y\)-coordinate is \(1\).

questions.concept: Sine equation with a negative value
questions.learningObjective: Solve a sine equation with a negative right side on one full turn in radians.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\sin x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), since \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV, so \(x=\pi+\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{4\pi}{3}\) or \(x=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{5\pi}{3}\). The angles \(\frac{7\pi}{6}\) and \(\frac{11\pi}{6}\) have reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) and sine \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Identify the reference angle for \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), then use the quadrants where sine is negative.

questions.concept: General solution when sine is zero
questions.learningObjective: Write the general solution of a sine equation with right side zero.
questions.question: What is the general solution of \(\sin x=0\), where \(k\) is any integer?
questions.explanation: The sine is the \(y\)-coordinate on the unit circle, which is \(0\) at both \((1,0)\) and \((-1,0)\). These points occur at \(x=0,\pi,2\pi,\ldots\), that is, at every multiple of \(\pi\). The formula \(x=2k\pi\) misses the solutions at odd multiples of \(\pi\).
questions.hint: Find every point of the unit circle that lies on the \(x\)-axis.

questions.learningObjective: Isolate the sine before solving a linear trigonometric equation.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(2\sin x-\sqrt{2}=0\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Isolate the sine: \(\sin x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\). The reference angle is \(45^\circ\), and sine is positive in Quadrants I and II, giving \(45^\circ\) and \(135^\circ\). At \(225^\circ\) the sine is \(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\); adding \(180^\circ\) is the pattern for tangent, not sine.
questions.hint: Solve for \(\sin x\) first, then use the reference angle in the correct two quadrants.

questions.learningObjective: Use the range of sine to decide whether an equation has solutions.
questions.question: How many real solutions does \(\sin x=2\) have?

options.label: A
options.text: None, because \(-1\le\sin x\le 1\) for every real \(x\).

options.label: B
options.text: Infinitely many, because sine is periodic.

questions.explanation: The sine is the \(y\)-coordinate of a point on the unit circle, so it always lies between \(-1\) and \(1\). The value \(2\) is outside this range, so no real \(x\) satisfies the equation. Periodicity repeats solutions only when at least one exists.
questions.hint: Compare the right side with the largest value that sine can take.

questions.concept: General solution of a sine equation
questions.learningObjective: Write both families in the general solution of a basic sine equation.
questions.question: What is the general solution of \(\sin x=\frac{1}{2}\), where \(k\) is any integer?
questions.explanation: In one turn the solutions are \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) and \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\). Sine has period \(2\pi\), so each solution repeats every \(2\pi\). The formula \(x=\frac{\pi}{6}+k\pi\) includes \(\frac{7\pi}{6}\), where the sine is \(-\frac{1}{2}\), and it omits \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\).
questions.hint: Find both solutions in one period, then add multiples of the period of sine to each.

questions.learningObjective: Count the solutions of a sine equation with a non-standard value in one period.
questions.question: How many solutions does \(\sin x=0.3\) have with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(0<0.3<1\), the horizontal line \(y=0.3\) meets the unit circle at two points, one in Quadrant I and one in Quadrant II. The solutions are \(x=\sin^{-1}(0.3)\) and \(x=\pi-\sin^{-1}(0.3)\). A calculator gives only the first, but the second is also in the interval.
questions.hint: The inverse sine gives one angle; ask whether another quadrant has the same sine.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a sine equation on an interval that includes negative angles.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\sin x=-\frac{1}{2}\) with \(-\pi\le x\le\pi\)?
questions.explanation: Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV, which correspond to negative angles in this interval. With reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{6}\), the solutions are \(x=-\frac{\pi}{6}\) and \(x=-\pi+\frac{\pi}{6}=-\frac{5\pi}{6}\). The angle \(\frac{7\pi}{6}\) has the correct sine but lies outside the interval because \(\frac{7\pi}{6}>\pi\).
questions.hint: Every answer must lie in the stated interval; replace an angle outside it by a coterminal angle inside it.

questions.learningObjective: Rearrange a linear equation in sine before solving it on one full turn.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(3\sin x+2=\sin x+1\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Collect terms: \(3\sin x-\sin x=1-2\), so \(2\sin x=-1\) and \(\sin x=-\frac{1}{2}\). The reference angle is \(30^\circ\), and sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV: \(x=180^\circ+30^\circ=210^\circ\) or \(x=360^\circ-30^\circ=330^\circ\). The angles \(30^\circ\) and \(150^\circ\) solve \(\sin x=+\frac{1}{2}\), which has the wrong sign.
questions.hint: Treat \(\sin x\) as a single unknown, solve the linear equation for it, and keep track of the sign.
